entities.summary: Ali Haydar, known as the "Father of the Syrian Special Forces", was a Syrian military officer who was the commander of the Syrian Special Forces for 26 years. He was a close confidant to President Hafez al-Assad and one of the members of Assad's inner circle. Born in the village of Hallet Ara, Haydar was a member of the Ba'ath Party from his youth. He was commissioned into the Syrian Army in 1952 after a stint studying at the Homs Military Academy. After the Ba'ath Party seized power in a 1963 coup d'état, Haydar was put in charge of Syria's special forces and supported al-Assad in his rise to the presidency.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ali Haydar played a crucial role in shaping Syria's military and political landscape for over two decades, serving as commander of the Syrian Special Forces from 1976 to 2002. His influence on President Hafez al-Assad's regime had significant regional implications.
